results.title: Smart forestry – a forestry 4.0 approach to intelligent and fully integrated timber harvesting
results.content: The field of technological implementation studies has undergone significant developments, with a notable emphasis on the advancement of digital tools, the establishment of data infrastructures, and the integration of artificial intelligence systems to facilitate the management and operation of forests [7,15]. Smart forestry is gaining global prominence as countries seek to modernize forest governance through digital technologies and data-driven approaches. Therefore, the goal of this study was to determine how business processes should be restructured to allow for a continuous use of forest machine data, with the main focus on harvester production data, along the German wood supply chain. * : Prabin Kumar DasPrabin Kumar Das. Digitalization of forest”, as this phrase itself suggests the sustainable implementation of cutting-edge technologies into forests for improving the current trends that are being used for forest environment monitoring, data acquisition, and analysis in the field of research and development. In addition to that, generalized architectures have been proposed which can be used directly in the future for advancements in research and development related to data collection and processing applications like flora analysis, forest fire predictions, etc. The role of digital technologies for fostering sustainability and efficiency in forest-based supply chains is well acknowledged and motivated several studies in the scope of precision forestry. Advanced planning systems can help to support decisions of the various entities in the supply chain, e.g., forest owners, harvest companies, haulage companies, and forest product processing industry. This paper analyzes contemporary literature dealing with digital technologies in forest-based supply chains and summarizes the state-of-the-art digital technologies for real-time data collection on forests, product flows, and forest operations, as well as planning systems and other decision support systems in use by supply chain actors. The increase of forest fires caused by the untenable exploitation has motivated the application of concepts such as Industry/Forestry 4.0 and Internet of Forest Things (IoFT) towards improving the performance of current supply chains and assuming an environmental responsibility. Furthermore, we discuss the latest developments of simulation modelling based on remote sensing data in forestry, which turns out to be the basis for the concept of a virtual forest as digital copy of the reality.

results.title: Best Practices for Using Digital Tools in Stakeholder Management: Expert Tips and Strategies
results.content: Explore how digital tools enhance stakeholder management for effective engagement and success. Explore how digital tools enhance stakeholder management for effective engagement and success. ## Understanding Stakeholder Management in the Digital Age. In the modern business environment, effective oversight of interested parties serves as a cornerstone of organizational success. The emergence of digital tools for stakeholder management, particularly participant coordination software, enables organizations to simplify interactions and promote transparency. By proactively involving interested parties through digital tools for stakeholder management, companies can cultivate stronger relationships and build trust—two critical components for successfully navigating challenges and driving sustainable growth. As organizations adopt digital tools for stakeholder management, they position themselves to capitalize on the latest trends and approaches in collaboration, which further enhances their operational effectiveness. Effective mapping of involved parties is crucial for success and can be enhanced by using digital tools for stakeholder management to recognize all relevant individuals while classifying them according to their influence and interest. By utilizing the Power/Interest Grid, which maps participants into four quadrants according to their level of power and interest, project managers can assess each individual's power and relevance, thereby leveraging digital tools for stakeholder management to prioritize engagement strategies. A well-organized participant matrix is among the digital tools for stakeholder management that serves as a valuable asset in this process. Engaging interested parties through tailored communication strategies—such as investor newsletters or feedback sessions for employees—utilizes digital tools for stakeholder management to ensure that their voices are recognized and integrated into strategic decision-making processes. Stakeholder Management" emphasizes that efficient oversight of involved parties, which includes the use of digital tools for stakeholder management, mapping, analysis, and interaction, directs leaders in their dealings with participants, resulting in improved decision-making and outcomes. This shift highlights the necessity of leveraging digital tools for stakeholder management to enhance engagement and communication with involved parties. As organizations navigate the complexities of technological evolution, the future of managing interested parties is poised for significant transformation through the adoption of digital tools for stakeholder management, alongside trends such as artificial intelligence (AI), big data analytics, and enhanced personalization.
